messages.author: a387d7985c232d82
messages.subject: Vectorized Count Model
parts:
Dear all,

I am fitting a binomial count model, where the counts are stored in R as a 3D array (group by question by time). The model runs fine in non-vectorized form, with the array of counts declared as follows:
  int<lower=0> RRY[G, Q, T]; // count of correct answers in group, by year
  int<lower=0> NNY[G, Q, T]; // count of responses in group, by year
and the response model written as follows:
  RRY[g, q, t] ~ binomial(NNY[g, q, t], prob[q, t, g]); // group counts
To speed up computation, I would like to vectorize binomial(), but this requires that I declare RRY and NNY as arrays of vectors, as in:
  vector[T] RRY[G, Q];
This causes an error, however, because binomial() requires that the response be integer type. I haven't come across any way to declare an integer vector, which makes me think that they are not supported. Is this correct? If so, is there any alternative way to vectorize this problem?

Thanks!
~Devin

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Vectorized Count Model
parts:
On 3/26/13 3:25 PM, Devin Caughey wrote:
>
> I am fitting a binomial count model, where the counts are stored in R as a 3D array (group by question by time). The
> model runs fine in non-vectorized form, with the array of counts declared as follows:
>
> int<lower=0> RRY[G, Q, T]; // count of correct answers in group, by year
> int<lower=0> NNY[G, Q, T]; // count of responses in group, by year
>
> and the response model written as follows:
>
> RRY[g, q, t] ~ binomial(NNY[g, q, t], prob[q, t, g]); // group counts
>
> To speed up computation, I would like to vectorize binomial(), but this requires that I declare RRY and NNY as arrays of
> vectors, as in:
>
> vector[T] RRY[G, Q];

Not quite. Here's the signature for binomial (from
the index):

binomial_log
(ints n, ints N, reals theta):real

An "ints" type means it can be an int or an int *array*,
and "reals" means it can be a real, real array, or real vector.

You're right that there are no vectors of int types.

There is a simple and then an extreme form of vectorization
you could do for this statement:
RRY[g, q, t] ~ binomial(NNY[g, q, t], prob[q, t, g]); // group counts

If you reorganize prob to be indexed prob[g,q,t], then you can
vectorize on t:

RRY[g,q] ~ binomial(NNY[g,q], prob[g,q]);

Or you could reorganize and vectorize on the longest dimension.

At a more extreme level, you can create one large G * Q * T array
and fill it in with your own indexing and vectorize that way.
It'll be more efficient, despite all the copying, but less readable.

RRY_vec int[G * Q * T];
NNY_vec int[G * Q * T];
prob_vec real[G * Q * T];
int pos;
pos <- 1;
for (g in 1:G) {
for (q in 1:Q) {
for (t in 1:T) {
RRY_vec[pos] <- RRY[g,q,t];
NNY_vec[pos] <- NNY[g,q,t];
prob_vec[pos] <- prob[q,t,g];
pos <- pos + 1;
}
}
}
RRY_vec ~ binomail(NNY_vec,prob_vec);

- Bob

parts:
You should not be getting a malloc error and crash no matter
what you do, so this is definitely a bug in our code somewhere.

Which version of RStan are you using? I'd like to try to isolate
the problem as an issue in RStan vs. Stan itself.

Could you send along the whole model? Feel free to send
it just to me (ca...@alias-i.com) if you don't want to share
with the world. Data would help to, but I can do without that.

You don't want to have to put these local variables in the
transformed parameter block where they'll be saved. You can
make them locals in one of two ways. You can declare them at
the top of the model block, as in

model {

int RRY_vec[T * Q * G];
int NNY_vec[T * Q * G];
int pos;

...compute values of RRY and NNY...
RRY_vec ~ binomial(NNY_vec, prob_vec);
}

or they need to be enclosed in their own curly braces within
the model:

{

int RRY_vec[T * Q * G];
int NNY_vec[T * Q * G];
int pos;

... compute values of RRY and NNY ...
RRY_vec ~ binomial(NNY_vec, prob_vec);
}

The curly braces define a block which determines the scope and local variables;
local variables can only be declared at the top of a block.

- Bob

Just to update everyone, Bob's second email identified the problem correctly: I had declared the local variables in the wrong place. Everything worked once I put them at the top of the model block.

~Devin
On Mar 26, 2013, at 5:48 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:

You should not be getting a malloc error and crash no matter
what you do, so this is definitely a bug in our code somewhere.

Which version of RStan are you using?  I'd like to try to isolate
the problem as an issue in RStan vs. Stan itself.

Could you send along the whole model?  Feel free to send
it just to me (ca...@alias-i.com) if you don't want to share
with the world.  Data would help to, but I can do without that.

You don't want to have to put these local variables in the
transformed parameter block where they'll be saved.  You can
make them locals in one of two ways.  You can declare them at
the top of the model block, as in

model {
 int RRY_vec[T * Q * G];
 int NNY_vec[T * Q * G];
 int pos;

 ...compute values of RRY and NNY...
 RRY_vec ~ binomial(NNY_vec, prob_vec);
}

or they need to be enclosed in their own curly braces within
the model:

{
 int RRY_vec[T * Q * G];
 int NNY_vec[T * Q * G];
 int pos;

 ... compute values of RRY and NNY ...
 RRY_vec ~ binomial(NNY_vec, prob_vec);
}

The curly braces define a block which determines the scope and local variables;
local variables can only be declared at the top of a block.

- Bob

On Mar 26, 2013, at 3:47 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com <mailto:ca...@alias-i.com>> wrote:

On 3/26/13 3:25 PM, Devin Caughey wrote:
>
I am fitting a binomial count model, where the counts are stored in R as a 3D array (group by question by time). The
model runs fine in non-vectorized form, with the array of counts declared as follows:
>
 int<lower=0> RRY[G, Q, T]; // count of correct answers in group, by year
 int<lower=0> NNY[G, Q, T]; // count of responses in group, by year
>
and the response model written as follows:
>
 RRY[g, q, t] ~ binomial(NNY[g, q, t], prob[q, t, g]); // group counts
>
To speed up computation, I would like to vectorize binomial(), but this requires that I declare RRY and NNY as arrays of
vectors, as in:
>
 vector[T] RRY[G, Q];

Not quite.  Here's the signature for binomial (from
the index):

binomial_log
(ints n, ints N, reals theta):real

An "ints" type means it can be an int or an int *array*,
and "reals" means it can be a real, real array, or real vector.

You're right that there are no vectors of int types.

There is a simple and then an extreme form of vectorization
you could do for this statement:

 RRY[g, q, t] ~ binomial(NNY[g, q, t], prob[q, t, g]); // group counts

If you reorganize prob to be indexed prob[g,q,t], then you can
vectorize on t:

 RRY[g,q] ~ binomial(NNY[g,q], prob[g,q]);

Or you could reorganize and vectorize on the longest dimension.

At a more extreme level, you can create one large G * Q * T array
and fill it in with your own indexing and vectorize that way.
It'll be more efficient, despite all the copying, but less readable.

 RRY_vec int[G * Q * T];
 NNY_vec int[G * Q * T];
 prob_vec real[G * Q * T];
 int pos;
 pos <- 1;
 for (g in 1:G) {
   for (q in 1:Q) {
     for (t in 1:T) {
       RRY_vec[pos] <- RRY[g,q,t];
       NNY_vec[pos] <- NNY[g,q,t];
       prob_vec[pos] <- prob[q,t,g];
       pos <- pos + 1;
     }
   }
 }
 RRY_vec ~ binomail(NNY_vec,prob_vec);

- Bob
